overview: Registry-based cohort of adults discharged alive after community-acquired pneumonia in 2016 to 2021, with five years of linked follow-up and two comparison groups.
population: All 11,800 registry patients discharged alive, first admission per person; comparison groups of general population adults matched four to one on age, sex and area, and adults discharged after urinary tract infection or cellulitis in the same hospitals and years.
exposure: Hospitalisation for community-acquired pneumonia; secondary exposure categories by severity score and by bacteraemia.
procedures: After approval, the statistics office links registry and comparison groups to the death register and regional admissions and returns a de-identified file. Frailty is calculated from admissions in the two years before the index date; follow-up starts at discharge and ends at death, leaving the region or five years.

outcomes.name: First cardiovascular event
outcomes.measure: Myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure admission or cardiovascular death, defined from hospital diagnoses
outcomes.timing: 0 to 1 year and 1 to 5 years after discharge
outcomes.why: The long-term risk clinicians believe persists (claim c1).

outcomes.name: All-cause death
outcomes.measure: Death from any cause from the national register

outcomes.name: Care home entry
outcomes.measure: First change of address to a registered care home among people living at home before admission

outcomes.name: Linkage completeness
outcomes.measure: Proportion of registry patients linked to both data sources

feasibility: Existing registry of 11,800 patients; linkage by the statistics office; analysis by one epidemiologist and a part-time statistician within twelve months of approval.
biasMitigation: Two comparison groups reported side by side
Frailty measured before the index admission
Complications of the index admission excluded from the main model

biasFlags.label: Confounding by frailty
biasFlags.note: Measured from prior admissions; residual confounding likely.

parsimony.simplestPath: One outcome, two windows, two comparisons, one covariate set.

theoreticalFramework: Target trial emulation to fix time zero at discharge and eligibility; no other framework.
summary: Registry cohort with one primary outcome in two windows, two comparison groups and care home entry as a secondary outcome.
